Obviously, since they've got a new manager and a fair few new players, it might take some time for them to start properly performing. But, to help them along the way, some transfers could be made to try and improve the performances of their first-team squad. item.title: Vincent Kompany to miss Bayern’s clash with Arsenal due to legs-affecting virus
item.description: Kompany told to rest after struggling with infection His assistant poised to oversee Champions League game Vincent Kompany is touch and go to be in the Bayern Munich dugout against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday night as he battles a debilitating virus that has affected his legs. Kompany was unable to attend his team’s training session on Tuesday before the Champions League tie, ceding the responsibility for the pre-match press conference to his assistant, Aaron Danks. Kompany has been told to rest after he struggled through Bayern’s 6-1 home win over RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga on Saturday, after which the club’s sporting director, Max Eberl, addressed the media instead of him. There have been reports in Germany that Kompany needed to lie down on his sofa at home after the Leipzig game and that the viral infection had affected an existing hip problem which meant he could hardly walk. item.description: Pakistan have won their first two matches in the tri-series, while England next play Sri Lanka on Thursday [Getty Images] One-day international tri-series, Rawalpindi Pakistan 302-9 (50 overs): Baker 3-65; Nawaz 79 (74), Arafat 59 (58) England 215 (38.4 overs): Banton 57 (53), Arafat 6-40 Pakistan won by 87 runs Scorecard England began their wandering winter with a sloppy loss to Pakistan in the one-day tri-series in Rawalpindi. In the opening match of five separate tours to four different countries on three continents, England's mistakes opened the door for Pakistan all-rounder Arafat Minhas to take advantage. The all-rounder made a crucial 59 with the bat, then bamboozled England by taking 6-40 with his left-arm spin. Asked to bat, Pakistan were 190-5 in the 37th over when diving wicketkeeper Jordan Cox put down Arafat on 12, one of three catches England dropped. Arafat, alongside a powerful 79 from Hasan Nawaz, lifted Pakistan to 302-9. Faced with making the second-highest score to win an ODI at the Rawalpindi Stadium, England made a rapid start to the chase, only for further errors to let Pakistan back in. At 91-0, Ben Duckett top-edged a pull to depart for 45 and, crucially, Tom Banton was caught for 57 when he shovelled Arafat's long hop to mid-wicket. Arafat's fine all-round performance continued with a beautiful delivery to bowl England captain Harry Brook for five and Naseem Shah got one to keep low to bowl Joe Root for 33. When Cox was lbw and Jamie Overton holed out, both off Arafat, England were flawed. item.title: ESPN star implores Arch Manning to enter the transfer portal
item.description: July 15, 2025; Atlanta, GA, USA; Texas quarterback Arch Manning listens to a question during SEC Media Days at the College Football Hall of Fame in Atlanta. Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning has had a rough couple of weeks. The Longhorns dropped their second straight game on Saturday, falling 27-24 to the Florida Gators at home, and Manning has faced no shortage of criticism for his backbreaking mistakes that continue to cost his team in critical moments. “We showed arrogance in believing that Arch Manning can do anything. And he almost did, except he finally got in the way of himself,” Finebaum said on The Matt Barrie Show , via Awful Announcing . “I came away thinking, I don’t know what this guy’s going to do. Because he is not the elite player that we all tried to make him out to be,” Finebaum added. “He can be great in moments, as we saw near the end of the game, as he threw that great play that set up the touchdown, but he can just be downright stupid in others.” NFL draft expert Mel Kiper Jr. went as far as to say that Manning, who came into the season widely expected to be the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft, is better off returning to college for a fifth year. “All I’ll say is right now, you’ve got to go back to college for another year,” Kiper on First Draft . “And if you don’t, it’s got to be the Green Bay Packer model of Jordan Love and Aaron Rodgers where you’ve got your guy and you’re picking late first round, and you’ve got your quarterback for another three years – I’m saying three years. I’m not saying one, I’m not saying two. “Patrick Mahomes sat for a year. Let’s forget the year. For Arch, I think it’s three years. It’s got to be the Jordan Love, Aaron Rodgers, Green Bay Packers model if he comes out.” Now, Kiper’s colleague at ESPN, Dan Orlovsky, is taking things a step further, and saying that not only should Manning return to school, but that he should enter the transfer portal and finish his collegiate career at a different school. “Arch should definitely go back to school (as of right now) and definitely not at Texas,” he posted on X on Tuesday. Arch should definitely go back to school (as of right now) and definitely not at Texas. @PaulHembo — Dan Orlovsky (@danorlovsky7) October 20, 2026 Kiper believes Manning needs to improve his consistency, and it would appear that Orlovsky just isn’t sure that the young quarterback is going to find that consistency under Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian, something another ESPN star, Paul Finebaum, would agree with. Monday night may have given the 49ers the one blow they can’t bounce back from: an Achilles injury to receiver Mike Evans. While it appears the Niners dodged a major bullet with Evans’ tendon remaining intact, it’s believed he will miss time while he recovers, with an estimated return following San Francisco’s Week 8 bye. That’s assuming there are no lingering issues, recovery goes perfectly, and he can get back to form immediately. Mike Shanahan’s most laudable trait as a coach is his ability to adjust to the hand he’s dealt, rather than let his team fail and make excuses after. Adjusting the injuries is nothing new for him, but when it comes to Mike Evans it might be the one injury Shanahan can’t mitigate. This season Evans isn’t just the No. 1 target for Brock Purdy, but far and away the most reliable receiver he has. Boasting a success rate of 69.2%, Evans is the key engine to the entire 49ers passing offense. Success Rate for a receiver is a metric that evaluates the impact of each reception, with a “success” defined as gaining 40% of required yards on 1st down, 60% on 2nd down, and 100% on 3rd and 4th down. We should view success rate as being synonymous with reliability or consistency. It’s about chain moving as much as anything else, and simply put: A 69.2% rate is obscene. A receiver having a solid season will be at or around the 50% mark, elite NFL receivers boast a success rate above 60%. This is consistent across the NFL. If we look at the league’s Top 15 receivers in yards, here are their associated success rates: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (SEA): 65.2% Chris Olave (NOR): 62.3% CeeDee Lamb (DAL): 55.1% Drake London (ATL): 57.4% Christian Watson (GNB): 52.1% Matthew Golden (GNB): 49.1% Malik Nabers (NYG): 50.8% Davante Adams (LAR): 57.1% Zay Flowers (BAL): 62.5% Tetairoa McMillan (CAR): 62.5% George Pickens (DAL): 53.8% Tee Higgins (CIN): 60.5% Mike Evans (SFO): 69.2% Garrett Wilson (NYJ): 56.3% Puka Nacua (LAR): 48.1% Other players typically regarded as brilliant include Justin Jefferson (58.3%) and Ja’Marr Chase (60.5%). We’re seeing that Evans is significantly better than every receiver in the NFL when it comes to his success rate, which is a huge factor why Purdy has been such a good quarterback this season. Evans is making life very easy for his quarterback. This has been his modus operandi since entering the league, but it’s particularly pronounced this year. Prior to 2026 the best success rate Mike Evans ever had was with the Buccaneers in 2024, at 62.7%. There’s no way to sugarcoat this one: As gifted as Shanny has been at coaching around adversity, Mike Evans is the single player he doesn’t have a way to coach around. Evans has been so good this season that this isn’t a case where San Francisco can dabble in the trade market and simply “find another receiver,” because another Mike Evans doesn’t exist anywhere else in the NFL. Any hopes of a Super Bowl this year for the 49ers hinges on their receiver returning from injury and back into form — it’s that simple.

item.title: Allen exits NI Open with Brown loss on return
item.description: Allen had not played since May's World Championship in Sheffield [Getty Images] Mark Allen's return to action ended in defeat as he became the latest big name to exit the Northern Ireland Open, losing to Jordan Brown at the Waterfront Hall. Allen, who had not played since his agonising World Championship semi-final loss to Wu Yize in early May, lost 4-2 to Brown in the all-Northern Ireland first-round contest in Belfast. Former world number one Allen becomes the 10th top-16 player to fall at the first hurdle this year, with Ronnie O'Sullivan, Judd Trump and Mark Selby among the early casualties. Allen, 40, took the opening frame on Tuesday afternoon but 39-year-old Brown hit back by taking the next two. While Allen levelled the match at 2-2, Brown built breaks of 53 and 80 in the final two frames to progress. In Tuesday's other early games, three-time world champion Mark Williams progressed with a 4-2 win over Robbie Williams, while Michael Holt knocked out Zhou Yuelong with a 4-1 victory. item.title: Max Verstappen defends Chris Lulham after online abuse
item.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen has issued a firm response in defense of his Verstappen Racing teammate Chris Lulham, after the British driver was subjected to a wave of online abuse following a race-altering collision at the GT World Challenge Europe season finale in Portimao. The incident occurred during the second hour of the three-hour Endurance Cup race on Saturday when Lulham, driving the #3 2 Seas Motorsport-prepared Verstappen Racing Mercedes-AMG GT3 he shared with the F1 driver and Ben Barnicoat, attempted a late move up the inside of Luca Stolz in the #48 Winward Racing car at the entry of Turn 8 on the first lap after a safety car restart. Contact ensued as Stolz turned in, sending the newly crowned Endurance Cup and combined GTWC Europe champion into a spin. Stewards deemed the move an avoidable collision and issued a drive-through penalty to the #3 car. Having been in contention for a podium finish, the penalty dropped Verstappen Racing down to 24th position before Verstappen mounted a late-race recovery stint to finish ninth. In the aftermath of the event, Lulham faced intense criticism and personal attacks on social media platforms, prompting Verstappen to address the situation directly on Instagram. "I feel it is necessary to address the hate and harassment Chris received after the race. Everyone is entitled to their own opinion about what happened on track, but these personal attacks are not okay," Verstappen said. "Chris put in a really strong stint, and mistakes happen. There is no place for this kind of behaviour in our sport or anywhere else." #3 Mercedes-AMG Team Verstappen Racing, Mercedes-AMG GT3 EVO Max Verstappen, Chris Lulham, Ben Barnicoat Despite the setback, Verstappen took a positive view of the overall weekend: "It was an exciting weekend! I was very happy to race with our GT3 car in Portimao. There were some highs and lows, but as a team we learned a lot." Lulham and Verstappen share a long-standing friendship built in virtual racing, having competed in countless sim racing events for Team Redline—now rebranded as Verstappen Racing. Verstappen’s long-term vision includes creating pathways for elite sim racers to transition into real-world motorsport, with Lulham representing the first driver to enter real competition under the initiative. Lulham expressed remorse over the clash with the Winward entry of Stolz, Maro Engel and Lucas Auer, while highlighting the team's recovery effort following a difficult qualifying session after a setup mistake. "A ninth-place finish at the end of a rollercoaster race that looked promising. Contact with the #48 resulting in a drive-through penalty took us out of the podium hunt. Apologies to them and for how it affected their weekend," the 23-year-old said. "It was a massive team effort to get the car turned around and on pace for Saturday's race after qualifying. A big thanks to the guys at 2 Seas Motorsport, Max Verstappen, and Ben Barnicoat." To read more Motorsport.com articles

item.title: Cardinals' coaching staff was on a rescue mission vs. Rams in Week 6
item.description: After an abysmal performance versus the Detroit Lions in Week 5, Arizona Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis was determined to have his unit prepared in Week 6. The Los Angeles Rams were spoiled 18-16 by what appeared to be a deflated Cardinals team, but Rallis and head coach Mike LaFleur put together the perfect scheme to rattle the stellar Rams offense. Rallis had received a hefty amount of the blame for the Cardinals' slow start to the 2026 season and another potential loss this past Sunday would've put him under even more scrutiny, yet Rallis has shown forth his brilliance helping the Cardinals to post mid-tier rankings in both sacks and interception totals. What the Cardinals have failed to do, however, is sustain offensive drives, a factor that has led to fatigue and forfeiture for the team defense. In Week 6, LaFleur was finally able to pack a punch with the ground game. Still, the Cardinals are near the top of the NFL ranks in time of possession per game, meaning that the teams' offense has been given many opportunities to turn drives into points. Rallis was focused on avenging the critics this past weekend and his unit held the Rams to just 16 total points, despite them having 10 total offensive drives. The Rams converted on just four of their 10 third-down conversion attempts and were limited to just 286 total yards on offense. The Cardinals rough-housed the Rams offense with 62 total tackles, four of them resulted in negative plays, and they also had seven hits on the opposing quarterback Matthew Stafford. Moving forward, expect Rallis and LaFleur to continue their relentless tread upward as the Cardinals aim to recover and rally their way back to above .500 before the midpoint of the 2026 NFL season. item.title: TGL unveils five-player team rosters for 2027 season
item.description: PALM BEACH GARDENS, FLORIDA - MARCH 24: A detailed view of a TGL presented by Sofi logo imprinted in the sand before the TGL presented by SoFi match between the Atlanta Drive GC and the New York Golf Club at SoFi Center on March 24, 2025 in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Cliff Hawkins/TGL/TGL via Getty Images) | TGL Golf via Getty Images TGL is ramping up. Monday saw the league have its first ever trade as Shane Lowry was dealt from The Bay Golf Club to Boston Common Golf. Within the announcement of Lowry’s move was the promise that each TGL roster would be expanding to five per team for the 2027 season, and we now know who will suit up for each squad. Los Angeles Golf Club: Collin Morikawa, Justin Rose, Tommy Fleetwood, Sahith Theegala, and Ben James Atlanta Drive GC: Chris Gotterup, Patrick Cantlay, Justin Thomas, Billy Horschel, and Michael Brennan The Bay Golf Club: Wyndham Clark, Min Woo Lee, Ludvig Aberg, Ryan Fox , and Blades Brown Boston Common Golf: Shane Lowry, Rory McIlroy, Keegan Bradley, Michael Thorbjornsen, and Hideki Matsuyama Jupiter Links Golf Club: Tiger Woods, Max Homa, Tom Kim, Akshay Bhatia, and Keith Mitchell New York Golf Club: Matt Fitzpatrick, Cameron Young, Rickie Fowler, Ben Griffin , and Alex Fitzpatrick Motor City Golf Club: Brooks Koepka, Jackson Koivun, Jake Knapp, Si Woo Kim, and Bud Cauley Those italicized are new to TGL, although everyone on Motor City Golf Club is new as they are the league’s first expansion franchise. Obviously Lowry has swapped teams as noted. There has always been a lot of star power within TGL and they are adding a ton of it with their new players this season, including some of the young and rising superstars on the PGA Tour. “Our teams are developing distinct identities that reflect their players’ personalities and competitive fire, the character of the cities they represent and the vision of their ownership groups,” said Rufus Hack, president, golf, TMRW Sports. “After two seasons, there’s history between these teams, and those growing rivalries bring added intensity to the competition. With Motor City Golf Club joining the league and new players bringing fresh energy to established teams, there’s plenty for fans to look forward to in 2027.” WTGL kicks off its inaugural season in short order, November 8th to be specific, so soon enough the SoFi Center is going to be rocking and rolling. Get ready.

item.description: CHILLICOTHE — The road to a Scioto Valley Conference cross country title still runs through Unioto High School. The Shermans won both the boys and girls races at Adena High School on Oct. 17, extending impressive streaks. Unioto's boys have now won 12 straight league championships, while the girls have claimed six consecutive titles. The top five finishers in the boys race were all Shermans. Corbin Scott finished first with a finish time of 16:06.4 while teammates Ethan Purtee (16:10.3), William Lynch (16:48.2), Rudy Leadingham (17:13.2) and Jayden Lewis (17:33.9) followed in order. The Shermans also received seventh, eighth and 10th-place finishes from Eli Good (17:47.0), Cameron Caplinger (17:50.7) and Justus Race (17:55.3). Adena's Carter Elliott finished sixth at 17:46.6, and Piketon's Emmitt Wallace was ninth with a time of 17:52.6. Team finishes and scores were as follows: Unioto (15), Westfall (74), Adena (78), Piketon (109), Paint Valley (142), Zane Trace (148) and Huntington (149). In the girls race, Huntington's Rachel Lute was the top finisher with a time of 21:28.7. item.title: Arsenal coach Arteta always a leader, says former teammate Gnabry
item.description: Mikel Arteta was Serge Gnabry's team-mate at Arsenal during the first few years of the Germany winger's career (Darren Staples) Bayern winger Serge Gnabry is not surprised former teammate Mikel Arteta became a successful coach, saying the Arsenal boss was always a leader in the dressing room. Gnabry, who started his club career at Arsenal, will go up against Arteta's Gunners at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday in the Champions League. "He was certainly a leader within our team back then. He was the captain during the season we played together," Gnabry told reporters on Tuesday. "I remember him helping us out. He shared a lot of advice with us. He was always very approachable and open. "That just goes to show what a kind person he is. He led the team to great success. It's not that we saw it coming, but he's clearly developed further and has done a fantastic job." The 31-year-old Germany international admitted it was "strange" to face a team coached by a former teammate, but added: "It's a special match for me -- playing against my former club. "The club where I spent many years, I grew up there from the age of 16." Bayern coach Vincent Kompany is suffering from a virus and may not be in the dugout. English assistant coach Aaron Danks took Tuesday's press conference and could step in for Kompany on Wednesday, but said there would be no extra personal motivation for the match. "I think it's always Bayern Munich's victory. I know Vince would be really strong on this, it's never about anybody's individual achievements, it's always about the collective, about the group," he said. "When you come to work with a club like Bayern Munich, you know it's much bigger than all of us." Kompany was on the sidelines for Saturday's 6-1 win over RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga but had difficulty walking and did not take the post-match press conference. Gnabry, who started his club career at Arsenal, will go up against Arteta's Gunners at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday in the Champions League. "He was certainly a leader within our team back then. He was the captain during the season we played together," Gnabry told reporters on Tuesday. "I remember him helping us out. He shared a lot of advice with us. He was always very approachable and open. "That just goes to show what a kind person he is. He led the team to great success. It's not that we saw it coming, but he's clearly developed further and has done a fantastic job." The 31-year-old Germany international admitted it was "strange" to face a team coached by a former teammate, but added: "It's a special match for me -- playing against my former club. "The club where I spent many years, I grew up there from the age of 16." Bayern coach Vincent Kompany is suffering from a virus and may not be in the dugout. English assistant coach Aaron Danks took Tuesday's press conference and could step in for Kompany on Wednesday, but said there would be no extra personal motivation for the match. "I think it's always Bayern Munich's victory. I know Vince would be really strong on this, it's never about anybody's individual achievements, it's always about the collective, about the group," he said. "When you come to work with a club like Bayern Munich, you know it's much bigger than all of us." item.title: Orioles' biggest offseason need revealed by MLB analyst
item.description: Orioles' biggest offseason need revealed by MLB analyst originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Orioles finished fourth in the AL East with a 79-82 record. They missed the postseason for the second consecutive season despite a stellar season from first baseman Pete Alonso. How can the Orioles ensure they don't miss out on the playoffs in 2027? FanSided's Zachary Rotman believes it starts with acquiring a frontline starting pitcher. An ace would be the best-case scenario. "Corbin Burnes gave the Baltimore Orioles ace production in 2024 and the O's, for whatever reason, have made no effort to acquire an ace since. "Trevor Rogers was their closest thing to an ace, and he's a free agent. Kyle Bradish is probably their best starter under contract right now, and he can be really good when he's on, but he's far too inconsistent to be relied upon as a frontline guy," Rotman wrote. The Orioles have a few starters that can put together several strong outings, but they are missing the star power up front. MORE : Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player "The Orioles need to improve the front of this rotation. Having a staff include the likes of Bradish, Shane Baz and Brandon Young is fine, as long as there is an ace pitching for them every fifth day," Rotman added. "They don't have that right now. Will Mike Elias be willing to splurge for one?" Of course, Baltimore's front office must be willing to spend money or offload prospects to acquire an ace. It won't be easy, but it may be necessary. item.title: U2 announced for NFL Thanksgiving Eve halftime show
item.description: Credit Robert Hanashiro-USA TODAY The NFL has owned Thanksgiving Day for decades, but now it’s laying claim to Thanksgiving Eve in an attempt to turn it into another marquee window. And this year they will have some assistance from U2. The iconic band has made multiple NFL appearances before. They famously played the halftime show of Super Bowl XXXVI in 2002 for the Patriots-Rams game, unfurling a moving tribute to the victims of the 9/11 terrorist attacks. They played in New Orleans again for another emotional show, this time during the pregame for the Saints’ return to the city after Hurricane Katrina in 2006. This year, the band will take center stage in Los Angeles during halftime of the Thanksgiving Eve game between the Rams and Green Bay Packers on Netflix, as the streamer announced on Tuesday. One of the biggest bands on the planet. One of the biggest stages in sports. U2 takes the field at halftime on Thanksgiving Eve during Packers vs. Rams — November 25 at SoFi Stadium and LIVE on Netflix. https://t.co/G4nJ19amr4 — NFL (@NFL) October 20, 2026 “There’s a reason U2 has headlined stadiums for decades: they don’t just perform; they deliver iconic moments audiences remember forever,” said Ted Sarandos, co-CEO of Netflix, in the announcement. “We’re thrilled that they’ll bring that same magic to the NFL stage on Netflix. After enduring his early-1951 slump and coming back to the majors that year, Mantle hadn’t hit his ceiling yet, but the world saw glimpses of what he would eventually become: the person in charge of carrying the torch after DiMaggio. Those were some big shoes to fill. No, Mantle wasn’t as classy as the ‘Yankee Clipper’, but he was a better player and a charismatic leader in his own way. Perhaps more importantly, he took the Yanks to a whopping seven World Series titles. The first one would come in that 1951 campaign, when he blew out his knee in Game 2 while giving DiMaggio room to make a play. That knee injury would shape everything that was to come, but Mantle of course found a way to excel, even with a bad knee. From 1952 to 1965, Mantle made the All-Star Game every year. He added two more Midsummer Classics to his resume in 1967 and 1968. His most impressive individual achievements, however, were the three AL MVP Awards he won in 1956, 1957, and 1962. His playing career continued until 1968, when he hit a rather disappointing .237, but with 18 homers and an excellent .385 OBP that gave him the foundation for a still-impressive 145 wRC+. Even in his last campaign as a major leaguer, he was an elite offensive performer. Mantle retired with a .298/.421/.557 line, 536 home runs, 153 stolen bases, 1,509 RBI, and 2,415 hits. Those who watched him in his early years say he could have stolen many more bases if it weren’t for the two major leg injuries he suffered. Mantle was a 20-time All-Star, a seven-time World Series champ, a three-time AL MVP, a Gold Glover in 1962, a batting champion in 1956, led the junior circuit in homers four times and in RBI in 1956. His number 7 is deservedly retired by the Yankees, and he has been a member of the National Baseball Hall of Fame since 1974. You can say with confidence that Mantle is one of the best players ever to play the game, and you can argue he might’ve finished even closer to the top of the list if it weren’t for injuries. According to the Society for American Baseball Research , “Mantle struggled to find a new career after retiring from baseball. He served as a Yankee first-base coach in 1970, but abandoned that rather quickly. He invested in a hotel and a restaurant chain, both of which eventually failed. In 1983, he was given a job in public relations with the Claridge Hotel and Casino in Atlantic City.” The booming baseball memorabilia industry gave his finances some much-needed life in the eighties. Unfortunately, he had to fight some demons during his life. He told family members and friends that he suffered from sexual abuse by his sister, Anna Bae, when he was a child. He had severe drinking problems, which eventually resulted in him being diagnosed with hepatitis and cirrhosis of the liver. It took him nearly his entire life to get sober, and shortly afterward, he was sadly diagnosed with liver cancer. “The Commerce Comet” passed away in August 1995, and the Yankees wore black armbands and a No. 7 on their sleeve to commemorate their fallen legend for the rest of the season. Mantle is, simply put, one of the greatest Yankees of all time. Maybe he wasn’t always a role model, but boy, could he play the game. See more of the “Yankees Birthday of the Day” series here .

item.title: Cadillac embraces American roots with bold Austin F1 makeover
item.description: Cadillac has revealed a special livery for the United States Grand Prix , introducing a new design inspired by the American West for its home race in Austin. The Formula 1 team's latest look combines its familiar black-and-white colours with intricate patterns inspired by traditional embroidery. Developed in collaboration with GM Design, the livery pays tribute to American craftsmanship and features several decorative elements across the car. The most noticeable changes can be found on the engine cover and around the cockpit, where white patterns have been added to the black bodywork. Similar detailing extends along the nose, while the white sidepods feature subtle designs surrounding the team's sponsors. Stars and Western-inspired illustrations also feature prominently, with the car number incorporated into the elaborate decoration on the engine cover. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Cadillac brings American West to Formula 1 The team explained that the design was intended to reflect its American roots, using traditional craftsmanship as the main inspiration for the special appearance. "The Cadillac Formula 1 Team comes home with a new look shaped by American craftsmanship," Cadillac stated on its official website. "Created in collaboration with GM Design, this special livery carries the character of the American West to the grid, weaving intricate embroidery and handcrafted detail into a design built for Formula 1." Cadillac also shared a series of images showing the car from different angles, offering a closer look at the patterns covering the bodywork. The contrasting black-and-white design remains the foundation of the livery, with the new elements adding further detail without significantly changing the team's established colour scheme. The American outfit also highlighted the importance of the occasion, describing the design as a way of bringing a distinctly American identity to the circuit: "There's an art to making an entrance. With intricate white embroidery against a sleek black canvas, this livery brings a distinctly American sense of style to a race on home soil." Cadillac's home weekend will also see American driver Colton Herta return to the cockpit for the opening practice session on Friday . The 26-year-old, who is competing in Formula 2 this season, will replace Sergio Perez for FP1, having already completed practice appearances in Barcelona, Hungary and Italy.

It's a fun World Series between two clubs that have never won a title before, which is great for the fans. However, as USA Today's Bob Nightengale outlined, this is a "nightmare" for Major League Baseball and TV executives. The reason why? It's thanks to a combination of likely lower ratings due to the smaller markets and what these low-payroll teams mean for a potential salary cap. Why Brewers vs. Rays WS matchup is a 'nightmare' for MLB and TV execs "It's a nightmare World Series matchup for Major League Baseball, which has stressed to everyone who'd listen that a salary cap is desperately needed, even running advertisements into the postseason," Nightengale writes. But since they both made the World Series and were clearly the best teams all season long, one of MLB's top talking points for why a salary cap is needed has gone out the window. item.title: FIFA says it will answer UEFA questions over Infantino controversies, but won’t say when
item.description: FIFA says it plans to address queries raised by European football’s governing body UEFA regarding Gianni Infantino ’s leadership, but has stopped short of promising a response before the candidacy declaration cutoff for next year’s FIFA presidential election. A letter from UEFA , viewed by the Press Association, sought clarity on a series of issues on behalf of European representatives on the FIFA Council by 2 November, 16 days before that candidate deadline. The delegates had challenged Infantino in person during a Council gathering in Zurich last week, before being instructed to put their concerns in writing. UEFA’s letter on Monday, sent from its secretary general Theodore Theodoridis to his FIFA counterpart Mattias Grafstrom, stressed that answers to questions around Infantino’s controversial World Cup private investor plan, United States President Donald Trump ’s influence over and involvement in FIFA’s business, plus a host of other topics could not be deferred until the next Council meeting, which is scheduled for 16 December. UEFA has lost confidence in Infantino over his handling of the World Cup private investor plan, and has said it will identify a credible alternative candidate to stand against him in next year’s election (AP) A FIFA spokesperson insisted replies would be given, but made no mention of whether that would be by 2 November. “The FIFA Governance Regulations state that Council meetings and their associated documentation are confidential,” the spokesperson said. “While FIFA intends to reply to questions submitted by its Council members it has no intention of breaching confidentiality by commenting on internal communication and/or documentation to media. “FIFA considers respect for these Regulations to be a function of respect for the Council itself and for its individual members. FIFA will always maintain this respect and will not be drawn into any exchange with any third parties that undermines this.” The UEFA letter sought answers on a wide range of topics, including the Folarin Balogun case, the World Cup final half-time show and the introduction of hydration breaks at the finals earlier this summer. item.title: Mike Garafolo still asking questions about what Jalen Hurts, Eagles were thinking letting him play with blood clot
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Mike Garafolo still asking questions about what Jalen Hurts, Eagles were thinking letting him play with blood clot appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles are facing uncomfortable questions about their handling of Jalen Hurts ’ medical emergency . NFL Network insider Mike Garafolo is still struggling to understand why the quarterback played against the Jacksonville Jaguars after an initial diagnosis of a superficial blood clot. Hurts is now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season after follow-up examinations revealed deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli. Garafolo questioned the decision-making process surrounding Philadelphia’s Week 5 game in London , particularly the timeline leading into kickoff. According to his account, Hurts spent hours at a local hospital. He then returned to the team hotel around 3-4 a.m., and was summoned again by 11 a.m. That sequence raised concerns about whether the quarterback had adequate rest before playing. Hurts skipped pregame warmups and carried the ball just twice in the Eagles’ 19-17 loss, adding another layer of uncertainty to the circumstances. From @gmfb on the Jalen Hurts blood clot, trying to fill in some gaps and why we still have questions that need to be answered. pic.twitter.com/GqXCvYENNs Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) October 20, 2026 “I keep coming back to nobody at any point up to and including Jalen Hurts himself said, ‘You know what, maybe this isn’t a good idea,’” Garafolo said. Philadelphia has relied on medical clearance, but the questions surrounding the decision are unlikely to disappear. With head coach Nick Sirianni offering limited public comment, scrutiny over the Eagles’ communication and medical protocols is growing. Hurts’ 2026 season began with promise before unraveling amid offensive struggles and now a serious health crisis. Across five starts, he recorded 933 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and three interceptions. The Eagles are currently in a four-game losing spiral, including that frustrating defeat to Jacksonville in London. The subsequent discovery of more serious blood clots has abruptly ended Hurts’ campaign. It has shifted the team’s focus from fixing its offense to protecting its franchise quarterback’s long-term health. item.title: Former Browns defender released by Titans due to ‘incident,’ won’t face former team in Week 7
item.description: The list of former Cleveland Browns in the NFL, as well as in other leagues , is quite expansive. Until recently, there were not always success stories on those lists, but Browns fans are passionate about anything and everything connected to their team, including former players (which is why we created our in-5 trivia daily game ). Cleveland’s matchup with the Tennessee Titans was supposed to bring about another blast from the past name: DT Jordan Elliott . The former Texas and Missouri prospect was selected by the Browns in the third round of the 2020 NFL draft, the first under current GM Andrew Berry. After four years in Cleveland, including 35 starts, Elliott signed with the San Francisco 49ers in free agency. After completing his two-year, $9 million contract, Elliott signed a two-year, $8 million deal with the Titans this offseason. After an “incident” at the facility, the Titans chose to release the veteran defensive tackle on Tuesday: The Titans announce they have released DL Jordan Elliott following an Oct. 15 “incident at the team facility.” — Jonathan Jones (@jjones9) October 20, 2026 The full statement from Tennessee on Elliott’s release: #Titans are releasing DT Jordan Elliott. Statement from the team: On Thursday, October 15, there was an incident at our team facility involving Jordan Elliott. Following our review of the incident, we have made the decision to release Elliott from our roster. We will have no… — TURRON DAVENPORT (@TDavenport_NFL) October 20, 2026 Elliott followed Robert Saleh, his defensive coordinator with the Niners, when he signed with the Titans, so the team’s head coach knew the player well. For the Browns, their Week 7 opponent just lost a defensive lineman who has played in 114 snaps so far this season. While Jeffrey Simmons is the big name on the Tennessee defense, Elliott was an important rotational player. Solomon Thomas, Nazir Stackhouse, Timmy Horney, and Jackie Marshall fill out the rest of the Titans defensive tackle depth chart.

item.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
